messages.subject: some problems about how to do a 3-step approach with tidyLPA in R
messages.subject_clean: some problems about how to do a 3-step approach with tidyLPA in R
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am using tidyLPA to finish my research, but I have some problems about produces after getting the latent profiles outcome. More specifically, I'd like to know how to run a 3-step approach in R after using the "estimate_profiles".

I find I could get the probability for each sample in CPROB* by using the code "get_data". I guess I could add these CPROB* as weights in the logit model, but I don't know how to add several weights in one logit model and I am not sure whether my assumption is right actually. Could you provide my some help?

Best,
Alisa

messages.subject: Re: Estimate_profiles not passing to plot_profiles
messages.body_plain:
Hey when I'm plotting my profiles I use this code:

plot_profiles(mydata, sd= FALSE, add_line = TRUE, bw= FALSE, rawdata = FALSE )

"my data" being the name of whatever I've saved the LPA solution I want to plot as.

Don't know enough to comment on your code but I hope this helps, has always plotted things for me.

PS: I have the following packages loaded:

library(tidyverse)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(kableExtra)
library(tidyLPA)
library(mclust)
library(rio)
library(dplyr)
library(foreign)
library(openxlsx)

messages.subject: LPA Scoring Equation
messages.body_plain:
I am hoping to generate a "scoring equation" from an LPA model that would allow us to classify a new case into one of the subgroups. In Latent Gold you can get coefficients for each indicator variable for each of the classes, and these coefficients can then be used to create a scoring equation. Is there a way to generate these coefficients using tidyLPA? Thank you! :)

Kimberley

messages.subject: Inconsistency in LMR Test in tidyLPA compared to Mplus
messages.subject_clean: Inconsistency in LMR Test in tidyLPA compared to Mplus
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am working on a project using latent class analysis in substance use disorders. While I began the project using R and your package to calculate the Lo-Mendell-Rubin Test, I’ve began to try to use Mplus, as it seems to be the standard for LCA in this area. However, when calculating the LMR Test with the same data in tidyLPA in R and Mplus, I get different results and I am not sure why.

I am wondering if it may be because the LMR Test are differently implemented or calculated between latent profile analysis and latent class analysis. If so, because the variables I am using are binary rather than continuous, and your package is designed to calculate the LMR test for LPA rather than LCA, might this explain why my results are different between tidyLPA and Mplus?

If this should not cause a difference, do you know what may be causing this discrepancy? I can provide further information if needed. Thank you in advance.

Brendan Stiltner (he/him)

Postgraduate Associate

Polimanti Lab (Division of Human Genetics)

Psychiatry Department, Yale School of Medicine
